content.value_statement: Stateful agent systems are hard to design, test, and debug. This skill provides LangGraph patterns for graph structure, state, routing, persistence, and human review.
actual_capabilities: Explains StateGraph construction with nodes, edges, START, and END routing.
Shows how to define typed state and reducers for accumulated data.
Demonstrates conditional branching for multiple workflow paths.
Describes tool integration through ToolNode and model tool binding.
Covers persistence concepts with checkpointers and resumable state.
Identifies anti-patterns such as infinite loops, stateless nodes, and monolithic state.
limitations: Examples focus on Python LangGraph usage.
Code samples are illustrative and need production validation.
LLM provider setup and credentials are outside the skill content.
It does not provide a complete deployed application.

use_cases.title: Prototype a ReAct Agent
use_cases.description: Create a small LangGraph agent that calls tools and loops until work is complete.

use_cases.title: Design Multi-Step Research Flow
use_cases.description: Plan shared state, reducers, and separate nodes for research, writing, and review.

use_cases.title: Review Agent Architecture
use_cases.description: Check an existing graph for exit conditions, state design, and routing clarity.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Agent
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a small tool-calling agent.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me a minimal LangGraph agent for one tool-calling workflow. Explain the state, nodes, edges, and stop condition.

prompt_templates.title: Design Shared State
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning for accumulated workflow data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design TypedDict state and reducers for a research assistant that stores messages, sources, findings, and errors.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Conditional Routing
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow design with multiple task paths.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a conditional routing plan for a LangGraph workflow that handles coding, search, and general chat requests.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Architecture
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before implementation or launch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my LangGraph architecture for production risks. Focus on persistence, human review, loop limits, error handling, and state boundaries.

output_examples.input: A developer asks for a first LangGraph agent design.
output_examples.output: The response outlines state, one agent node, one tool node, routing logic, and a clear end condition.

output_examples.input: An architect asks how to split a research workflow.
output: A suggested graph separates research, writing, and review nodes.
The state plan explains which fields accumulate and which fields overwrite.

output_examples.input: A team lead asks for a production readiness review.
output_examples.output: The response checks loop limits, persistence, human approval points, error handling, and state size.

best_practices: Define clear state fields and use reducers only when values must accumulate.
Add explicit END routes, loop counters, and timeout controls.
Keep nodes focused and return only the state fields they update.
anti_patterns: Using eval or unsafe dynamic execution in tools.
Building loops without a clear exit condition.
Putting unrelated data into one large shared state object.

faq.question: Does this skill build complete LangGraph apps?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and examples that developers adapt to their application.

faq.question: Which language does it focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on Python LangGraph usage.

faq.question: Can it help with ReAct agents?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a ReAct-style agent graph with tools and conditional routing.

faq.question: Does it cover persistence?
faq.answer: It lists checkpointers and persistence as production concerns, but examples remain high level.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Is every code sample production safe?
faq.answer: No. Review examples before use, especially any tool that evaluates user-provided input.
